label: Real run on this Mac's Docker Compose stack, with synthetic traffic from klaxon.traffic: synthetic data, a simulated provider, no real money. One fault from klaxon.faults, duplicate-delivery, was injected on purpose. The alert was raised by klaxon.alerts from what the stack showed. Klaxon's loop ran live on it, through Claude Code on Aravind's seat, and stopped on diagnosed after 10 steps; any reply it got is a recorded response, not a simulation. It was offered one write action (rollback_deploy), as in week 4; in an evaluation run its gate only plans an action the diagnosis names: nobody is asked, and nothing runs. The diagnosis was compared with the fault's recorded cause by a rule (klaxon.grading), not by a person or a model. Code planned the action its diagnosis named (redeploy ledger-consumer: LEDGER_HANDLER naive -> idempotent, LEDGER_BAD_EVENTS dead_letter (unchanged)); in an evaluation run nobody is asked, and nothing ran. The fault's cause was removed by the harness's clearing (klaxon.faults).

diagnosis.hypothesis: ledger-consumer was recreated at 18:24:07Z with LEDGER_HANDLER=naive. Since then it books every Kafka message as a new ledger transaction, with no dedupe on provider event_id. The provider redelivered evt_000281 ($157.18 charge, pay_000259) and evt_000368 ($18.25 refund, pay_000324). This is normal at-least-once behaviour that the ledger must tolerate. webhook-receiver does no dedupe, so it queued each delivery as its own message: offsets 120/121 and 152/153. The ledger posted all four. The duplicate charge put pay_000259 $157.18 ahead of the provider. The alert at 18:24:24Z saw only that duplicate. The evt_000368 duplicate came later, at 18:24:35Z, and put pay_000324 $18.25 behind. Settled, provider_clearing is +$138.93. payment-confirmer did not change the payment twice (already_confirmed), so only the ledger is wrong.

evidence.shows: Settled check: evt_000281 is posted twice (transactions 281 and 282) and evt_000368 twice (369 and 370). provider_clearing is +13893 cents = 15718 - 1825. Payments and refunds match the provider, and the ledger is balanced, so the books hold duplicate transactions and the money is not lost.

ledger-consumer is the only service recreated after 18:22:41Z: at 18:24:07Z, with LEDGER_HANDLER=naive. That is 5s before the first duplicate. payment-confirmer runs CONFIRMER_HANDLER=by_our_id, unchanged.

ledger-consumer logged 'posted' for evt_000281 twice: from provider-events/1@120 at 18:24:12.374Z and from @121 at 18:24:12.886Z, with different trace ids. That timing comes after the 18:24:24Z alert's predecessor duplicate and explains the alert's $157.18.
webhook-receiver received evt_000281 twice, about 0.5s apart, and queued it at offsets 120 and 121. It passes duplicates straight to Kafka.
evt_000368 follows the same pattern. The ledger posted it from offsets 152 and 153 at 18:24:35.191Z and 18:24:35.694Z. This came after the alert fired, which is why the alert reported only $157.18.

The first evt_000281 delivery was acked 200 in 3.5ms, so the redelivery was not caused by a failed ack. The ledger did a plain INSERT INTO transactions (outcome posted) with no event_id guard. The confirmer's conditional UPDATE ... WHERE status='pending' returned already_confirmed.

proposed_fix.summary: Roll ledger-consumer back to the settings it ran before the 18:24:07Z deploy, presumably a LEDGER_HANDLER that dedupes on event_id. This stops new double-posts. Then, separately and with human sign-off, repair the data: reverse or delete the duplicate transactions 282 (evt_000281) and 370 (evt_000368) and their entries. Re-run money_check to confirm all five invariants pass. Longer term, add a unique constraint on transactions.event_id so that no handler setting can double-post.

diagnosis.blast_radius: The ledger-consumer container is recreated, so ledger posting pauses briefly. Its consumer group resumes from committed offsets, and events queue in Kafka meanwhile, with no loss. The previous handler is not visible in these results. If it was not dedupe-safe, or the rollback target is wrong, duplicates continue. Code refuses the rollback if the deploy log has no prior deploy. The rollback does not fix the existing duplicates ($157.18 and $18.25 rows). Those need a separate data repair. Any other redelivered events posted between 18:24:35Z and the rollback would also need repair.
diagnosis.rollback_plan: If the rolled-back ledger-consumer misbehaves, for example by failing to post or erroring on events, redeploy it with the current settings (LEDGER_HANDLER=naive, BAD_EVENTS=dead_letter) and look for another handler that dedupes. Do the data repair as compensating ledger entries rather than deletes, so it can be undone by reversing them. Re-run money_check after each step.
